claim: The XGBoost fraud detector is ready for production deployment because it meets every quantitative acceptance bar set in CLAUDE.md while flagging 82 of 98 true frauds with high precision.
evidence: F1 = 0.8586387434554974 on the held-out 56,962-row test set (metrics.json), clearing the CLAUDE.md deployment bar of F1 >= 0.85.
AUC = 0.9683850045364235 (metrics.json) indicates near-ideal ranking separation between fraud and non-fraud.
Precision = 0.8817204301075269 (metrics.json); the confusion matrix [[56853,11],[16,82]] shows only 11 false positives out of 56,864 legitimate transactions, keeping customer friction negligible.
Recall = 0.8367346938775511 (metrics.json) - 82 of 98 actual frauds caught on the test split.

Trained on 227,845 rows with stratified 80/20 split (pipeline_output.json train_test_split) using scale_pos_weight=577.2868020304569 (metrics.json hyperparams), properly correcting for the 0.001727485630620034 fraud rate from eda_summary.json.

Model exploits strong, PCA-orthogonalised signals: V17 |corr|=0.3265, V14 |corr|=0.3025, V12 |corr|=0.2606 (eda_summary.json top_features), giving a defensible feature basis rather than spurious patterns.
challenges: pipeline_output.json reports drift_detected=true (max_abs_rel_delta=2.000 on V3 per trace.jsonl drift-monitor entry), so production performance may degrade without retraining cadence.
Only 98 fraud cases in the test set means F1 is estimated on a small positive support; a single attempt (metrics.json attempts=1) was run with no cross-validation.
Recall of 0.8367 means ~16% of frauds are missed, which may be unacceptable for high-value transactions without a human-in-the-loop review queue.
